title: UPDATE: Police sniper shot, killed suspect in Vaughan hostage situation
article: A police sniper shot and killed the suspect in the Dec. 13 hostage situation at a Vaughan bank, a police source said.

"The SIU investigation is going to be focused on the interaction between police officers and the individual. Of course, as part of that investigation we're going to look to determine what happened in the lead up to that event," said Jason Gennaro, a spokesman for the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), which investigates interactions between police and civilians that result in serious injury, death or allegations of sexual assault.
York Regional Police responded shortly after 1 p.m. Dec. 13 to the RBC near Major Mackenzie Drive West and Dufferin Street after receiving reports that a man was carrying a weapon.
The bank is in a small strip mall, Eagles Nest Village Plaza, on the northwest side of the intersection.
There were reportedly more than a dozen people inside the bank when officers arrived.
Police managed to get some of those people out, but a number - five, according to some media reports, 13 according to others - were held inside, by the suspect, a 25-year-old Vaughan man.
Negotiators were called to the scene, but in the end, police used "lethal force," a police spokesman said.
According to the SIU, two police officers shot at the man, who was struck and killed.
"It was the only way we could gain control of the subject," Const. Andy Pattenden said, adding it wasn't immediately clear if the man was attempting to rob the bank.
The owner of the Esso station next door to the bank described the moment the hostages were brought out, their hands tied with cable.
"They looked frightened," said Maatn Arasaratnai. "I've never seen anything like this."
Businesses at plaza, including the Playcare Early Learning Centre, were evacuated and the occupants were loaded on to a York Region Transit bus.
The people from the bank, meanwhile, were loaded onto an EMS bus.
Aside from the suspect, no one was seriously physically injured.
"I can tell you they're definitely traumatized," Pattenden said. "This would have been a very traumatic event and we're going to do everything we can to help these people."
One business owner from the plaza across the street called it "frightening".
"That's our bank," Pancer's Deli Emporium owner Frank Houston said. "I know the manager and there's a daycare there, so it's frightening."
Major Mackenzie Drive, between Dufferin Street and Peter Rupert Avenue, was closed until about 1 a.m., causing traffic gridlock for several hours.
"It's insane," said an employee at a hair salon on the east side of Dufferin Street, who declined to give her name. "It's crazy to think this could happen in this area. We thought it was safe."
The employees and customers were inside the business with the door locked, with some of the customers checking their phones for details about the incident.
